items.title: SOE Seminar Series | THE AI DISRUPTION: The Future of Work, Human Potential, and the Power to Adapt | Tuesday, November 10, 2026
items.body:
Reminder: The SOE seminar
*THE AI DISRUPTION: The Future of Work, Human Potential, and the Power to Adapt
*by Dr. Anwar El-Homsi will take place tomorrow, Tuesday, November 10, at 12:30 p.m., at the Chagoury Medical Auditorium, Byblos Campus.

We look forward to seeing you all there!

Greetings,

As part of the
SOE seminar series, the School of Engineering is pleased to invite you to the semester entitled “THE AI DISRUPTION: The Future of Work, Human Potential, and the Power to
 Adapt”.

The seminar details are as follows:

🎤
Speaker: Dr. Anwar El-Homsi, LUMINAH.AI CEO

📄
Title: THE AI DISRUPTION: The Future of Work, Human Potential, and the Power to Adapt

📅
Date: Tuesday, November 10, 2026

🕒
Time: 12:30 p.m. – 01:30 p.m.

📍
Place: Chagoury Medical Auditorium, Byblos Campus

We look forward to seeing you all there!

Abstract:

Artificial Intelligence is transforming the world at an unprecedented pace, reshaping industries, redefining professional roles, and challenging traditional approaches to education, work, and
 problem-solving. For the next generation of engineers, understanding this transformation is no longer optional; it is essential to preparing for the future of their profession.

This presentation explores how AI is changing the nature of work. It examines the implications for engineering and other professions, highlighting the distinction between automating individual
 tasks and transforming entire occupations. It also considers the current capabilities and limitations of AI, emphasizing the continuing importance of human judgment, creativity, critical thinking, curiosity, and accountability. Beyond understanding the disruption,
 the presentation focuses on the opportunities it creates. It advocates a new model of professional development in which strong engineering fundamentals are complemented by AI literacy, interdisciplinary thinking, adaptability, and the ability to collaborate
 effectively with intelligent systems.

About the Speaker:

Dr. Anwar El-Homsi is a global AI innovator, distinguished technologist, and founder of LUMINAH.ai, an advanced AI-driven innovation platform focused on solving humanity’s most complex challenges
 in clean energy, particularly nuclear fusion, high-efficiency solar materials, and carbon-neutral energy infrastructure. With a career spanning more than 30 years, he has led breakthrough work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, energy systems,
 applied statistics, and engineering, helping organizations accelerate scientific discovery and build future-ready technologies.

Dr. El-Homsi has contributed to major Fortune 100 companies and advanced R&D organizations, including Cisco Systems, Verizon, Corning, Eastman Kodak, Becton Dickinson, Heidelberg Digital, Xerox,
 Harris Corporation, Wilson Greatbatch, and Space Systems Loral. His leadership roles have centered on AI strategy, innovation ecosystems, digital transformation, Lean Six Sigma excellence, and scalable product development. As a consultant, he has advised corporations
 such as Bombardier, Bausch & Lomb, JPMorgan Chase, Excellus BlueCross, and Gamesa, guiding them through high-impact innovation, operational optimization, and emerging technology integration.

A prolific inventor, Dr. El-Homsi has authored over 10 AI-related patent applications, including systems for autonomous AI agents, computational design, responsible AGI, and advanced energy technologies.

items.title: Recognizing students’ global leadership: Millennium Fellowship
items.body:
Dear Students,

The United Nations Academic Impact and Millennium Campus Network (MCN) proudly present the
Millennium Fellowship.

The program convenes, challenges and celebrates bold undergraduate students advancing the
Sustainable Development Goals on campus and in communities. As a Millennium Fellow, you will hone your skills, take concrete action and earn recognition. There is no cost for selected students.

Undergraduate students can apply by the next priority deadline:
November 30, 2026. The class of 2027 will run from August to December 2027.
items.blurb: The United Nations Academic Impact and Millennium Campus Network (MCN) proudly present the Millennium Fellowship.

items.title: Library Monthly spotlight: LAU's Poster collection
items.body:
Dear LAU Community,

The LAU Libraries is home to some amazing resources! In our October spotlight, we will bring some of these resources straight to your inbox.

 This month's spotlight resource is....

What?  LAU's Poster collection

Who can benefit?  Anyone who is interested in graphic design, the history of theater at LAU, or is just looking for
 a bit of LAU nostalgia.

How to access?

-
 LAU:
 School of Arts & Sciences. Dept. of Communication Arts:\(Major Productions\) — 65 posters documenting major theatrical and musical productions.
-
 LAU.
 School of Arts & Sciences. Dept. of Communication Arts:(Student
 Productions\) — 314 posters showcasing the creativity and artistic achievements of LAU students.
-
 LAU
 Poster Collection \(donated by Rami Al Khal\) — 56 historical posters documenting activities associated with BUC, BCW, and LAU.

Hungry for more?  V isit the
LAU Libraries Archives & Special Collections  page
 to explore these collections and discover the stories preserved through these remarkable posters.
